title: Design Your Personal Action Plan
description: Outline your next 90 days of accessibility learning and advocacy.
problemStatement:
## Your 90‑Day Accessibility Plan

Create a personal action plan for the next three months. Include:

- **Learning goals**: what topics you'll deepen (e.g., ARIA, screen reader testing, legal compliance).
- **Practical tasks**: audit a project, fix 5 accessibility bugs, build an accessible component.
- **Advocacy**: give a lightning talk at work, write a blog post, mentor a colleague.
- **Community involvement**: join a11y Slack, attend a meetup, follow experts on social media.
- **Certification prep** (optional): if interested, outline steps toward IAAP CPACC.

Write in a structured format (list or table). Be specific and realistic.
hints: Schedule time blocks in your calendar.
Set measurable goals (e.g., 'Fix all contrast issues on my portfolio by March 15').
solutionCode:
# My 90‑Day Accessibility Action Plan

## Month 1: Foundations & Audit
- [ ] Complete the WebAIM Screen Reader Survey report reading.
- [ ] Audit my personal website with axe DevTools and manually (keyboard + VoiceOver).
- [ ] Fix all critical and serious issues found.
- [ ] Watch 2 Deque University videos on accessible JavaScript.

## Month 2: Deepen Skills
- [ ] Build an accessible combobox component and test with NVDA.
- [ ] Write a blog post about my audit experience.
- [ ] Give a 10‑minute accessibility lightning talk at the team meeting.
- [ ] Participate in the A11y Slack community.

## Month 3: Advocacy & Certification Prep
- [ ] Create an accessibility checklist for my team's PR reviews.
- [ ] Mentor one junior developer on semantic HTML.
- [ ] Register for the IAAP CPACC exam and start studying 1 hour/week.
- [ ] Attend an accessibility meetup (virtual or in‑person).

## Weekly Habits
- [ ] Read the a11y Weekly newsletter.
- [ ] Spend 15 minutes navigating a site with a screen reader.
- [ ] Look at one new WCAG success criterion each week.
